name: Galaxy Surfactants Ltd
title: Galaxy Surfactants Ltd - 540935 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Document is the Q1 FY26 call transcript (Aug 2025), not Q2 FY27 as labelled; volumes +5% YoY, EBITDA/MT flat at INR20,000 vs 20,200, with tariff-driven US ordering hesitancy.

summary.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY26: consolidated volumes up 5% YoY and EBITDA up ~4.5% to INR135 crore, with EBITDA/MT flat-to-lower at INR20,000 vs INR20,200 a year earlier.
summary.overview: Consolidated volumes rose 5% YoY and 9% QoQ, split evenly between Performance and Specialty care. EBITDA grew about 4.5% YoY to INR135 crore (vs INR129 crore), while EBITDA per metric ton was INR20,000 against INR20,200 a year ago. India volumes were up 3% YoY and 15% QoQ, and AMET was flat YoY but up 5% QoQ, with Egypt and Turkey weak. Rest of World grew close to 16% YoY, while US tariff uncertainty made Premium Specialty customers in North America cautious. Management said feedstock (LA/fatty oil) prices remain elevated and expects a correction, though timing is uncertain.

financial_highlights.change: Evenly split between Performance and Specialty care
vs INR129 crore in Q1 FY25, about +4.5% YoY
vs INR20,200/MT a year ago; reported as down sequentially by about INR5/kg on gross margin per kg (analyst figure)
LATAM and APAC led; Americas close to double digit

segments.name: Performance Surfactants (India/domestic)
segments.commentary: Customers are reengineering formulations to cut costs under high feedstock prices; management called this tactical and said EBITDA/MT on these products is similar to current India products. India volume +3% YoY, +15% QoQ.

segments.name: Premium Specialty (North America)
segments.commentary: Subdued in Q1 as customers suspended orders during US tariff uncertainty; Tri-K business was challenging. Management said the current order book remains healthy.

segments.name: Premium Specialty (Europe)
segments.commentary: Flat in tonnage but with a richer product mix, per management.

segments.name: AMET
segments.commentary: Flat YoY and up 5% QoQ; Egypt and Turkey markets remain subdued, offset by growth in other African, Middle East and Turkey-adjacent markets.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Brightest segment at close to 16% YoY growth, driven by LATAM and APAC.

guidance_outlook: Management is not targeting 8% volume growth; it would be happy with 4% growth (last year's level) for FY26 and 6% on a lower guided range. Getting to 6% to 8% would be difficult unless India demand recovers significantly.
India full-year growth depends on the festive season; management said the first half will show whether demand has returned.
Expects feedstock prices to correct, timing and extent uncertain. Management said that a sharp fall could be dramatic and is managing raw material positions tactically.

Expects the time-lag effect on pricing to fade if prices stay stable at current high levels, with margins potentially returning to last year's Q2 and Q3 levels; demand remains a constraint at high prices.
Capex for FY26 and FY27 is limited to debottlenecking and maintenance projects of about INR120 crore to INR150 crore; no significant new projects while tariff and geopolitical uncertainty persists.
US exports to be rerouted from Egypt where possible to mitigate the 50% tariff scenario discussed by analysts.
capex_capacity: Maintenance and debottlenecking capex guided at INR120 crore to INR150 crore for FY26 and FY27; no major new investments in the near term.
Management clarified that the INR2,000 crore five-year capex figure raised by an analyst was not announced by the company; it was only a capital allocation discussion under Strategy 2030.
Two new subsidiaries formed, one in Europe and one in Latin America/US, to access markets.
Mexico EPC services project started about two months before the call; no margin or revenue detail given yet.
demand_pricing: Feedstock (LA / fatty oil / fatty alcohol) prices remain high, up roughly 100% per management; supply from a key Southeast Asian supplier was disrupted in Q1 and is easing.
Pass-through lags price increases; management said the company is passing through prices, with a timing difference, and EBITDA/MT dipped due to product mix and North America order suspensions.
Customers are shortening purchase horizons from 6 months to about 3 months, and buying patterns vary by segment and risk appetite.
Regional Tier 2 players are squeezed between multinationals and agile Tier 3/D2C brands, per management.
Customer data: Tier 3 revenue up about 45%+ YoY, Tier 1 up about 25%, regional players up high single digit (analyst figures).
Egypt: an integrated local competitor is gaining share, limiting the company's addressable market there.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin per kg fall about INR5 QoQ despite 20-25% YoY revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a timing lag in passing on higher raw material costs, not a structural issue. The EBITDA/MT dip was attributed to product mix and suspended US Premium Specialty orders.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company passing on raw material price cuts quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers expect immediate pass-through on price falls, but the company will manage inventory positions carefully to avoid bloated high-cost inventory.

qa_highlights.question: How big is US exposure and how will tariffs be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: US is about 8% to 10% of the portfolio. Management plans to route more supply from Egypt (which has some specialty production) and will absorb some tariff impact where margin allows, while supporting customers temporarily where it does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in India versus peers' volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India grew 3% YoY (described as flattish) and 15% QoQ, and customers are managing costs and pipelines tightly. The festive season is the key test.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vision 2030 target of 2x volume and 2.5x EBITDA a change in strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in strategy and declined to give a detailed answer on the call, offering a separate discussion instead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the right to win against BASF and Croda in US and Europe Specialty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 45 years of experience, capability and teams, and two new subsidiaries in Europe and LATAM/US; it also said the company will engage both MNC and smaller D2C customers.

risks_watch: US tariffs (cited as high as 50% in analyst questions) could hit North America Premium Specialty and Tri-K demand, and possibly lead to reformulation or downtrading.
Feedstock price correction could be sharp; inventory positions carry mark-to-market risk if prices fall fast.
Egypt and Turkey headwinds and competition from an integrated local player.
India demand recovery depends on the festive season; customers are cutting pipelines and reformulating.
Shipping congestion in Europe, China and Southeast Asia is raising lead times.
summary.management_tone: Confident on resilience and the Rest of World and India sequential recovery, but cautious on US tariffs and India demand. Evasive on the Vision 2030 volume target and the capex figure raised by analysts, and deferred several questions to a separate discussion.
key_quotes: Our consolidated volumes rose 5% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter, an outcome that was evenly distributed between our Performance and Specialty care segments.

EBITDA per metric ton, though has been maintained at the same levels as last year at INR20,000 per metric ton versus INR20,200 per metric ton levels despite the various challenges that we had during the quarter.
We anticipate feedstock prices to correct and are hence managing our raw material price risk in a very calibrated manner.
So I'll be very happy if I'm able to keep my last year growth of 4% continued in this year, okay?
